clue.text: Wise man cheesemongers associate with Derby

definitions.meaning: ... Derby is an English cheese marbled green with ... leaves

explanation.definitionFit: A sage is a wise man, and the herb gives its name to the green-veined Sage Derby cheese sold by cheesemongers.

clue.text: In desert, see Bedouin dance

indicators.note: the nomad sits inside the desert word, so 'In' places one piece within the other

parts.note: sand is what a desert is made of; a sandy waste
a Bedouin is a nomadic Arab

explanation.surface: Watch a nomad perform a traditional dance out in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is only a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: A saraband is a slow stately Spanish dance in triple time.

clue.text: Lanky guy initially plying the rod

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word guy is wanted

parts.note: using a fishing rod is angling

explanation.surface: A tall thin fellow is out fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangling describes someone tall, thin and awkward, a synonym of lanky.

clue.text: Posh individual thus goes about, moving very fast

indicators.note: the word for thus surrounds the other pieces, going about them

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as printed
U means upper-class, posh, in the old social labelling
an individual is a person

explanation.surface: A snooty person rushes around at high speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Supersonic means travelling faster than sound, so moving very fast.

clue.text: Greek character set up, swindled and ruined

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are raised, so read upwards

parts.note: nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet
to do someone is to cheat or swindle them

explanation.surface: A Greek was framed, cheated and left destitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Undid in the sense of brought to ruin or downfall, as in 'pride undid him'.

clue.text: Rudimentary plant all but consumed by odd mice

indicators.note: the plant goes inside the rearranged rodents, eaten up by them
odd suggests strange, so the letters of mice are rearranged
every letter of the plant except the final one is kept

parts.note: bryony is a climbing hedgerow plant

explanation.surface: Peculiar mice have nibbled away almost all of a young plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' asks for the rodents' letters to be scrambled and 'all but' drops the plant's last letter; 'consumed by' sets the shortened plant inside the scramble. Bryony is a climbing hedgerow plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Embryonic means at an early, undeveloped stage, which is rudimentary.

clue.text: One's slander can go miles when spread about

indicators.note: spreading things about scatters them, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Gossip travels a long way once it gets passed around.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'One's' is a link; 'when spread about' rearranges SLANDER, CAN, GO and M.
explanation.definitionFit: Here 'One' stands for a person, and the whole clue describes a gossip who spreads slander far and wide.

clue.text: Comparatively torpid musical item

definitions.meaning: more numb, the comparative of numb
a song or piece in a show or concert

explanation.definitionFit: Read as numb-er it is more numb; read normally it is a song in a performance.

clue.text: Stick with this as a source of light?

definitions.text: Stick with this as a source of light?

parts.words: Stick with this as a source of light?
parts.note: add this word before stick and you have a holder for a wax light, so the stick goes with it to give illumination

explanation.definitionFit: A wax light is put on a stick to make a candlestick, and it is itself a source of light.

clue.text: Began again to tear round one of the Cotswoldsp, for example

indicators.note: the word for tear goes round the sheep

parts.note: to rend is to tear apart

parts.words: one of the Cotswoldsp, for example
parts.note: the Cotswold is a breed of sheep, so one such animal might be a ewe; the stray p is a scanning slip for Cotswolds

explanation.surface: Someone resumed tearing around the Cotswold hills.
explanation.walkthrough: Cotswold here is the sheep breed, not the hilly area of England; the stray p in the clue as held is a scanning error.
explanation.definitionFit: Renewed can mean resumed or began again, as in 'renewed the attack'.

clue.text: Wife at church dance constrains son to proceed cautiously

indicators.note: the dance holds the letter for son within it

parts.note: the one-step is a ballroom dance

explanation.surface: A wife at a church dance keeps a firm hold on her son.
explanation.definitionFit: Watch one's step is an idiom meaning take care or act cautiously.

clue.text: He may have a smack at escorting bishop round island

indicators.note: at accompanies the earlier letters by following them

parts.note: b is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a round shape is the letter O
Man is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Someone likely to be slapped is accompanying a bishop around an island.
explanation.walkthrough: A smack is a small fishing boat, not a slap.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatman works a small boat, and a smack is a kind of fishing boat.

clue.text: Took food at last, filling stomach after usual time

indicators.note: the meal pieces go inside the stomach, filling it

parts.note: belly is another word for stomach
to eat is to take food, past tense ate

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word food is taken

explanation.surface: Someone finally ate, filling an empty stomach well past mealtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Belatedly means late, after the expected or usual time.

clue.text: Live in luxury with duke?

parts.note: to live well is to live in comfort and luxury

explanation.surface: A duke enjoys a life of luxury.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to live in a place, to reside.

clue.text: Casually taking name, call Anthony to order

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone offhandedly takes a name and summons Anthony.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonchalantly means in a calm, unconcerned, casual way.

clue.text: North European youth conceals plot to crush monarch

indicators.note: in a down answer the upper part sits on top of the monarch, crushing it
the youth hides the scheme within himself

parts.note: a lad is a youth
a plot is a plan or scheme
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch

explanation.surface: A young man is hiding a scheme to overthrow the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A Laplander is a native of Lapland in the far north of Europe.

clue.text: Subject for newspaper

definitions.meaning: a citizen or subject of a country
a paper circulated across the whole country

explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a state, and a national is also a countrywide newspaper.

clue.text: One represents English supporter in social engagement

indicators.note: the pieces go into the engagement word

parts.note: a date is a social appointment
a leg supports a table or a body

explanation.surface: An English backer attends a social function as a representative.
explanation.definitionFit: A delegate is one chosen to represent others, as at a conference.

clue.text: Bug quietly installed, make speech for examiners

indicators.note: the soft letter is placed inside the bug

parts.note: a bug is an insect
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to orate is to give a speech

explanation.surface: Someone plants a listening device and then makes a speech to the inspectors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' looks like a spy device but means an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspectorate is a body of inspectors, that is, examiners.

clue.text: Very best advice leads to drug being given up

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice

indicators.note: in a down clue, given up means sent upwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Advice to quit drugs is the best there is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being given up' looks like quitting but turns POT into TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiptop is an informal word for excellent, of the very best quality.

clue.text: I am in costume in city of the republic

indicators.note: the phrase goes inside the clothing word

parts.note: wear means clothing, as in evening wear
I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: Someone in fancy dress is visiting a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Weimar is the German city that gave its name to the Weimar Republic of 1919 to 1933.

clue.text: Entries made by accountant, also once by son

parts.note: item is an archaic word for also, used formerly to introduce each entry in a list

explanation.surface: An accountant's entries, as well as those a son once made.
explanation.definitionFit: Items are individual entries in an account or list.

clue.text: Next to part of the perimeter of a large triangle?

definitions.text: part of the perimeter of a large triangle?
definitions.meaning: read as three words, one lengthy edge of a big three-sided figure

explanation.definitionFit: Alongside means beside, and split up it describes a long edge of a triangle.

clue.text: Area in very large island providing sanctuary

indicators.note: the letter for area goes into the size abbreviation

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a very large size

explanation.surface: A region of a huge island offers refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a place of refuge or sanctuary, literally a fertile spot in a desert.

clue.text: Drawn to link casual worker with 1950s youth

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker
a Ted, Teddy boy, was a British 1950s youth in Edwardian-style dress

explanation.surface: A temporary worker is paired with a teenager of the fifties.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were British youths of the 1950s who wore Edwardian-style suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempted means attracted or drawn towards something.

clue.text: Shrub that's no good in Asian republic

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes into the country's name

parts.note: Syria is a republic in western Asia

explanation.surface: A bush that will not thrive in a Middle Eastern country.
explanation.definitionFit: Syringa is a shrub genus, the lilac, also used for mock orange.

clue.text: Analyse a harp arrangement in this free rendering

indicators.note: the rearranged instrument goes inside the word for analyse

parts.note: to parse is to analyse grammatically

indicators.note: an arrangement reorders the letters, as in music

explanation.surface: A musician analyses a harp arrangement as a loose interpretation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' turns A HARP into APHRA; 'this' is a link pointing to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A paraphrase restates a text freely in other words.

clue.text: Red-headed Australian Tory?

definitions.meaning: Australians jokingly nickname a red-haired person Bluey or ...
the Conservative Party's colour stands for a Conservative

explanation.walkthrough: Australians perversely call a redhead Blue; in Britain blue is the colour of the Conservative (Tory) Party.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang a redhead is called this colour, and in Britain it marks a Conservative.
